mara.activity: Wake, drink water, open the curtains, and sit at the edge of the bed to sort the market, nursery, presentation, and family priorities.
mara.intention: Begin deliberately rather than letting the deadline dictate the whole day.

mara.activity: Wash up, brush my teeth, dress for errands, and gather my tote and wallet.
mara.intention: Get ready efficiently for the market and nursery.

mara.activity: Make coffee and eat a quick breakfast at the kitchen island while reviewing only the three presentation decisions that still need an answer.
mara.intention: Keep the deadline in a contained morning review instead of beginning another full work session.

mara.activity: Go to the farmers market and plant nursery for produce, herbs, and a small number of replacement plants and supplies.
mara.intention: Complete the usual Saturday errands without adding unnecessary browsing or new design decisions.

mara.activity: Return home, place my keys deliberately in the open entryway while removing my shoes, carry the field notebook to the living room sideboard countertop, and bring the market herbs to the kitchen.
mara.intention: Reset the arrival points so the afternoon does not begin in clutter.

mara.activity: Wash the produce, trim the houseplants, put the herbs in a glass beside the sink, and reset the kitchen surfaces.
mara.intention: Restore a calm, usable kitchen before the relative settles in.

mara.activity: Assemble a simple lunch and set it out, then eat at the island and leave the kitchen ready for later use.
mara.intention: Offer practical hospitality without turning lunch into an elaborate production.

mara.activity: Welcome the relative, show them the guest room and bathroom, and make the shared spaces comfortable while keeping the office and presentation materials private.
mara.intention: Create a generous arrival without surrendering the whole house or my work rhythm.

mara.activity: Make one protected final presentation pass at the office desk, checking hierarchy, planting quantities, image captions, and file naming; leave the fabric samples and planting sketches on the desk shelf when finished.
mara.intention: Make the remaining judgments coherent and defensible, then stop before perfectionism expands the task.

mara.activity: Close the laptop, carry it and the project folder out of the work area, and make tea before settling into the living room.
mara.intention: Mark a real transition away from the deadline.

mara.activity: Read and sketch garden ideas with tea, allowing the relative's conversation to remain easy and brief rather than trying to solve every familiar question.
mara.intention: Return to beauty and curiosity after the practical work is complete.

mara.activity: Put the book and sketch materials on the living room coffee table, straighten the seating, and check whether the relative needs anything before taking a quiet break.
mara.intention: Be attentive while preserving a small pocket of privacy before evening.

mara.activity: Eat a light, uncomplicated dinner and wash my own plate and utensils afterward, leaving the kitchen orderly rather than hosting a second meal.
mara.intention: Keep the evening sustaining and low-pressure while Julian is occupied with service.

mara.activity: Take a quiet shower and change into comfortable clothes, keeping conversation with the relative warm but bounded.
mara.intention: Recover from the long day and protect the transition into night.

mara.activity: Sit in the piano hall with the lights low and play a few slow scales, then leave the music area quiet.
mara.intention: Let the remaining mental pressure settle without reopening the presentation.

mara.activity: Return to the bedroom, wash up, brush my teeth, and prepare the bed for sleep without checking work messages.
mara.intention: End the day cleanly and avoid feeding the deadline overnight.

mara.activity: Read quietly in bed, then place my reading glasses on the top of my nightstand.
mara.intention: Close the day with something restorative and familiar.
Rest before the next day of presentation and family obligations.

julian.activity: Wake quietly, wash, brush my teeth, and get dressed in comfortable clothes while the house is still settling.
julian.intention: Start slowly and conserve energy before a long workday.

julian.activity: Carry a mug to the kitchen, grind coffee, and make toast with butter and honey. I bring the mug and toast to the kitchen island and make easy conversation with the visiting relative without getting drawn into a long morning discussion.
julian.intention: Be welcoming while keeping breakfast uncomplicated.

julian.activity: Carry the mug and plate to the sink, rinse them, and wipe the island around my breakfast. I leave Mara room for her market departure and do not start a larger kitchen task.
julian.intention: Clear only what I used and protect the morning's quiet rhythm.

julian.activity: Collect my backpack, chef jacket, and knife roll. I check my phone, wallet, keys, watch, and restaurant notebook, tucking the receipts back inside the notebook, then carry the thermos from beside the sink and fill it before leaving.
julian.intention: Pack methodically so I do not improvise or forget something after a late night.

julian.activity: Travel to the restaurant and handle prep, deliveries, and kitchen management. I check the Saturday stock, organize the incoming goods, set the prep list, and keep the kitchen ready for the evening team.
julian.intention: Get the kitchen safely and calmly through prep despite the long service ahead.

julian.activity: Travel home, carry the thermos into the kitchen, and set it beside the sink. I put my backpack down, wash my hands, and change out of the work layers.
julian.intention: Mark the end of prep and reset my body before returning to the restaurant.

julian.activity: Eat something small and familiar from the refrigerator, then sit with the visiting relative for a short, affectionate conversation. When the questions begin circling, I excuse myself kindly and leave my phone alone for a few quiet minutes.
julian.intention: Offer company without spending all my remaining energy before service.

julian.activity: Change into my restaurant shirt and work trousers, put on my kitchen clogs, and gather my backpack and knife roll. I collect my wallet and earplugs from the living room coffee table and take the keys from the piano's middle shelf.
julian.intention: Dress and gather everything in one deliberate pass before leaving again.

julian.activity: Travel back to the restaurant and review the service notes before the doors open.
julian.intention: Arrive with enough margin to breathe and give the team clear instructions.

julian.activity: Run dinner service and closing duties. I keep the line moving through the rush, make the necessary calls rather than improvising alone, supervise storage and cleaning, and finish the final checks after the last guest leaves.
julian.intention: Lead a demanding Saturday service steadily and safely.

julian.activity: Travel home, carry the thermos into the kitchen, and set it beside the sink. I put my backpack down, drop my wallet and earplugs on the living room coffee table, and wash my hands.
julian.intention: Get home without creating another job for myself.

julian.activity: Take a hot shower, dry off, and change into sleep clothes without turning on the television. I leave the towel in the bathroom to deal with later.
julian.intention: Let the heat bring me down from service and avoid unnecessary decisions.

julian.activity: Carry a bowl and fork to the kitchen, eat a small portion from the refrigerator with a glass of water, then rinse the bowl and fork and leave them beside the sink.
julian.intention: Put a little food in my stomach before sleep without cooking.

julian.activity: Brush my teeth, carry my phone charger to the nightstand, and put my phone down to charge. I get into the main bedroom bed beside Mara.
julian.intention: Finish the familiar post-service routine and go straight to sleep.
Recover from the long Saturday service.
